Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time shut down, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and TV tracking app called Bingers, focusing on social features. Details are as follows.

Bingers is now available for download.

The TV tracking app TV Time was previously shut down by Whip Media. One of its co-founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as a "fast, beautiful, and community-driven watchlist".

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering a "spiritual successor" for users still looking for a TV Time alternative—TV Time was once one of the most popular TV tracking apps worldwide.

Users who were originally TV Time users and saved their data through the official export tool before the platform shut down can import their archived data into Bingers and continue using it seamlessly. As for users who did not export their data, or new users who have never used a TV tracking app before, they can start from scratch and build their own viewing records.

Bingers heavily emphasises its community-driven features, such as user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity elections. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features are precisely why TV Time has been so popular for years:

For users who simply want to record the shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlists and viewing records. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays upcoming programme schedules, listing premiere dates and counting down how many days until broadcast.

Bingers is now available for free download on the App Store, and currently does not offer any in-app purchases.
